He couldn't fly a plane. So he built one. Full size.
Kaiyuan, northeast China. Zhu Yue was a farmer, then a welder.
Around forty, he realised he'd never fly. He couldn't buy a plane, but he could build one.
His blueprint? A toy Airbus, eighty times smaller.
With five friends, he welds a full-size A320. Thirty-seven metres long.
Sixty tonnes of steel. Over two and a half million yuan of his savings.
It has a cockpit, spinning engines, even stairs to board.
One problem: it will never fly.
So he wants to turn it into a restaurant. Thirty-six first-class seats, and a red carpet.
In China, if you can't buy the dream, build it. Find yours at laowai dot ma.
